title: Acyclicity of direct image from one affine open
statement:
Let $A$ be a commutative ring, $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ a separated scheme
morphism [def-pc-morphism-conventions], $W\subseteq X$ an affine open with inclusion
$j:W\to X$, and $\mathcal F$ a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. The module
category has injective resolutions [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Then
$j_*(\mathcal F|_W)$ is $f_*$-acyclic [def-sp-acyclic]:
$R^q f_*(j_*(\mathcal F|_W))=0$ for every $q>0$. No finite cover, complex,
augmentation, or derived-category isomorphism is part of this statement.

source.place: Proof, paragraphs 2 and 3, before the finite-product argument

proof.text: By separatedness over an affine base, intersections of affine opens are affine [lem-weil-pbc-separated-affine-open-intersection]. Hence the open inclusion j is affine. The composite f j is affine because its source and target are affine. Restriction preserves quasi-coherence. Apply [lem-pc-affine-morphism-hi] to j and f j to get vanishing of their positive higher direct images of F restricted to W.

Restriction to W is an exact left adjoint of j_*, so j_* preserves injectives. The module categories are Grothendieck abelian [prop-pur-kinjective-resolutions-exist]. Thus (j_*, f_*) is a composable pair [def-sp-composite-acyclicity] sending injectives to f_*-acyclic objects. The spectral sequence [thm-sp-grothendieck] has only its q=0 row by the first step. All differentials touching that row vanish, and its finite abutment filtration has one possibly nonzero graded piece, so R^p f_*(j_*F|W) is isomorphic to R^p(f j)_*(F|W). The latter vanishes for p>0 by the first step. Empty W and zero F give zero direct images.
